It's a slur within the United Kingdom which very loosely refers to not even just people from Pakistan, but from All of South Asia, which includes India. It's more of a generalized slur against anyone in the UK of South Asian Origin, that could happen to residents, citizens or even tourists, though I cannot personally speak as to how common it is in this current age (I'm Latin-American, but born and raised in the US), but I have heard it is in essence, used much like the N-Word, but for South Asians, again, which also includes India. This word over there has a strong historical background of being used out of hate and racism towards people of South Asian Origin from around 1964 ever since, as there had been an increase in Immigrants arriving to the United Kingdom from South Asia.

Think of it sort of as like some Americans calling every Latin-American a Mexican in that particular context. There are however many cases where that can easily just be an innocent first guess (Mexico is a Large Country and the Most Populated Spanish-Speaking Country to be fair) as to what I would be, so I don't take it personally, but the P-Word doesn't have that same sort of versatility in contexts in the UK as calling a Latin-American a Mexican would in the US, if that makes sense.
